title: Samsung Health Makes Sleep Coaching Easier To Start and Tailors Weekly Guidance
text: Samsung Electronics today announced a major update to the Samsung Health app, making Sleep Coaching 1 even easier to start by lowering the data requirement to begin. The update also delivers more personalized sleep guidance and expanded running program tiers to help users build lasting, healthier routines. Sleep Coaching Becomes Easier To Start and More Personalized While sleep tracking tells users how they slept, sleep coaching helps them sleep better by turning personal sleep goals and data into daily habits. Samsung has made it even easier to begin sleep management. Users can now initiate Sleep Coaching with just three days of data within the past two weeks instead of seven days in a month. During setup, users complete a survey on sleep regularity, sleep interruptions, alcohol and caffeine intake, and subjective sleep satisfaction. With these survey responses and three days of sleep data, the app assigns a personalized Sleep Animal symbol and builds a tailored four- to eight-week coaching program based on individual goals. As users progress, the program dynamically adapts its weekly recommendations to reflect changing sleep patterns, tracking daily sleep satisfaction and lifestyle shifts. Informed by principles of behavioral sleep science, the program gives users daily habit checklists and sleep tips — making it easier to build healthier routines, such as avoiding screens an hour before bed, skipping late caffeine, and stretching outdoors after waking up. Users can also enjoy more intuitive and detailed analysis reports. The new pentagon-shaped Sleep Balance graph consolidates five key aspects of sleep indicators — sleep time, sleep regularity, awake time during the night, sleep satisfaction, and Energy Score 2 — to provide an at-a-glance view of sleep trends and areas that may warrant attention, based on data collected or inputted through sleep coaching. Morning daily insight messages, which review the previous night’s sleep with helpful tips, integrate closely with weekly and final reports to provide a comprehensive view of sleep trends. By linking daily actions with this data-driven progress, Samsung Health helps users establish sustainable lifestyle habits to support everyday wellness. Expanded Running Programs and Strava Routes Integration In response to the growing popularity of running, Running Coach 3 has been upgraded to deliver a more dynamic and connected training experience. Training tiers have expanded from 10 to 12 levels. While users continue to receive a personalized training plan based on a 12-minute running test or their historical running data, this update introduces new levels to support intermediate and advanced runners. These dedicated training tiers enable them to set higher benchmarks, challenge themselves, and steadily improve their performance. To celebrate achievements and sustain motivation, Running Coach introduces an enhanced social media sharing feature. Runners can seamlessly export their workout data into share-ready templates designed for various social platforms, making it easier to share milestones, personal records, and route highlights with their fitness communities. Samsung continues to strengthen ecosystem connectivity through a partnership with Strava, 4 a global fitness platform. Users can import their favorite Strava Routes for running, trail running, and cycling directly into Samsung Health. This integration supports compatibility and user convenience across both platforms. “Samsung Health’s personalized coaching empowers users to understand their health data, taking a step toward supporting everyday wellness,” said Hon Pak, Senior Vice President and Head of the Digital Health Team for the Mobile eXperience Business at Samsung Electronics. “We will continue to leverage the Galaxy ecosystem and our technology to build a trusted health platform.” These upgraded features will be progressively rolled out via Samsung Health app updates starting in October. 5 Available on Samsung Health App v.6.24 or above and must be paired with Samsung Galaxy smartphones with Android OS 11 and above. Requires a minimum of three days of sleep data tracked within a seven-to-14-day period. Available via Galaxy Watch 4 series and later models, Samsung Galaxy Fit3 and later models, and Samsung Galaxy Ring. ︎ To check the Energy Score, the health data tracked from Samsung Galaxy Watch or Samsung Galaxy Ring must be synchronized with the Samsung Health App. The result is for your personal reference only and is not intended for medical purposes. ︎ Running Coach is available on Android phones (Android 10 or above) and requires Samsung Health app (v6.30.2 or above). Samsung account login required. Service available only with Galaxy Watch8 Series or later Galaxy Watch Series. ︎ Strava is available worldwide, excluding Belarus, China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Russia, parts of Ukraine, and South Korea ︎ Some features may be supported through future software updates, and availability and timing may vary by market, model, and other conditions. ︎

title: Samsung Art Store Expands Its Collection With 30 Exclusive Works From the British Museum
text: ▲ “A Storm (Shipwreck)” by Joseph Mallord William Turner on The Frame Pro Samsung Electronics today announced that it is adding a new exclusive British Museum collection consisting of 30 artworks to Samsung Art Store. 1 Available on compatible Samsung Art TVs, the curated selection features works by John Constable, Joseph Mallord William Turner, and other renowned artists. The collection includes Constable’s English countryside vistas, famous for the artist’s rare ability to portray shifting weather patterns in the sky. Turner’s watercolors, on the other hand, range from stormy seascapes to views of Venice, Rome, and Zurich. “Samsung is committed to using our technology to make world-class art more accessible to everyone,” said Gwiho Lee, Executive Vice President of the Visual Display (VD) Business at Samsung Electronics. “By welcoming these iconic British Museum pieces into our platform, we are proud to offer our global audience an effortless way to appreciate historic art at home.” ▲ “Fisherton Mill” by John Constable on The Frame Pro Samsung Art Store subscribers will have access to the British Museum collection and will be able to simply browse the selection, choose a work to display on their TV, and switch to another work whenever they like. “We’re delighted to work with Samsung to make more of the Museum’s collection available to people at home,” said Lisa San Martin, Interim Commercial Director of the British Museum. “We hope it encourages viewers to explore works they already know and discover others for the first time.” The launch builds on Samsung’s relationship with the British Museum. Samsung is also a corporate partner of the museum’s “Korea” exhibition that opened on Oct. 1 and runs through Jan. 31, 2027. The British Museum collection will be available on Samsung Art Store starting Oct. 6. About The British Museum Founded in 1753, the British Museum was the first national public museum in the world. From the outset it was a museum of the world, for the world, and this idea still lies at the heart of the Museum’s mission today. The collection tells the stories of cultures across the world, from the dawn of human history, over two million years ago, to the present. Objects range from the earliest tools made by humans and treasures from the ancient world to more recent acquisitions from Africa, Oceania, and the Americas, the Middle East, Asia, and Europe, as well as the national collections of prints and drawings, and coins and medals. Samsung Art Store subscription required. Subscription fees apply. Artwork availability and collection contents are subject to change at any time without notice or user notification. ︎

title: Samsung Introduces ‘SmartThings Now’ in New Platform Update That Brings More Intuitive User Experiences
text: Samsung Electronics today announced the latest update to SmartThings, its global connected living platform now serving 470 million registered users and supporting 430+ Works with SmartThings (WWST)-certified brands worldwide. The update introduces SmartThings Now at the top of the Home tab, refreshes the app’s Home tab experience, and expands local control capabilities — helping users access relevant information, take action more easily, and manage connected devices with greater reliability. “This update marks another step in SmartThings’ ongoing efforts to move beyond a home experience where users search for and launch features,” said Jaeyeon Jung, Executive Vice President and Head of the SmartThings Team, AI Platform Center, Samsung Electronics. “By delivering relevant information and controls at the right time, SmartThings is pushing the boundaries of more intelligent home experiences and empowering users to manage their everyday lives more naturally.” A Redesigned Home Tab Experience, Led by SmartThings Now SmartThings Now appears as cards at the top of the Home tab, building on Home Insight to offer greater personalization by combining relevant information with actions users can take right away. It suggests the right information and immediately actionable controls based on the user’s current situation, delivering an experience that is easier and more intuitive. title: Lee Kun-Hee Collection Expands to Europe With Opening of ‘Korea’ Exhibition at the British Museum
text: Samsung Electronics, in partnership with the British Museum, hosted a gala event on Sept. 30 at the museum to commemorate the opening of “Korea” exhibition, a major showcasing of works from the late Samsung Chairman Lee Kun-Hee’s renowned art collection. Following successful exhibitions in Washington D.C. and Chicago, it marks the European stop of the collection’s international tour. It is also the first major special presentation of Korean art at the British Museum in more than 40 years. The exhibition runs from Oct. 1, 2026 to Jan. 31, 2027, and is being held at the Joseph Hotung Great Court Gallery. “Korea,” spanning over two millennia, connect the history of Korean art in a unified narrative to reveal how Korea’s unique aesthetic values and artistic achievements have continued to be built upon and reinterpreted over many generations. The exhibition, drawn from over 23,000 artworks from the National Bequest of the Lee Kun-Hee Collection in 2021, is organised by the British Museum, the National Museum of Korea, and the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea. At the gala, Samsung Electronics Executive Chairman Jay Y. Lee reflected on the Lee family’s multigenerational commitment to preserving Korea’s cultural heritage and sharing it with audiences around the world. Members of the family, including Hong Ra-Hee, Director Emerita of the Leeum Museum of Art, Lee Boo-jin, President & CEO of Hotel Shilla, and Lee Seo-hyun, President of Samsung C&T, also attended the event. “For generations, my family has held a guiding principle that art and culture should be preserved and shared,” Executive Chairman Lee said. “I hope this exhibition offers a gateway into Korean culture, spanning two thousand years of creativity and heritage, and that it will let everyone see Korea a little differently — for its beauty, its depth and its resilience.” At the reception held before the gala dinner, Her Royal Highness The Princess Royal graced the opening of the exhibition. Among the 240 guests were the Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey MP, Minister for Artificial Intelligence Kanishka Narayan MP, former Deputy Prime Minister Sir Oliver Dowden, former Trade Minister Sir Greg Hands, former Culture Secretary Sir John Whittingdale, Trade Envoy to the Republic of Korea John Slinger, Leader of the Liberal Democrats and Chair of the Republic of Korea All-Party Parliamentary Group Sir Ed Davey, and Dr. Ben Spencer, Vice Chair of the Republic of Korea All-Party Parliamentary Group. George Osborne, Chair of the British Museum, said, “We are thrilled here at the British Museum to be hosting this incredible exhibition. The Lee family’s contribution to our shared cultural heritage helps us understand and interpret the past, so that we may understand the future.” Maurice Lévy, Chairman Emeritus of Publicis Groupe, said that the exhibition is “not simply about objects from witnesses of a great past of Korea. They are evidence of a culture that has always valued craftsmanship, imagination, discipline, and excellence. Sharing those treasures with the world speaks volume about the values and the generosity of the Lee family. They understood, generation after generation, that looking forward does not mean forgetting where you come from.” Kanishka Narayan, Minister for Artificial Intelligence, said, “The UK and Korea work closely on technology and innovation, but there is so much more to our relationship. Korea’s art and culture are admired around the world, and this exhibition gives people in Britain a chance to explore its extraordinary artistic heritage. I’m grateful to Samsung for bringing this remarkable collection to London and sharing it with audiences here.” Kim Heung-chong, Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to the U.K., commented that “it is particularly meaningful for the British Museum to open this exhibition of artworks showcasing two thousand years of Korean history, at a time when K-culture is enjoying global recognition,” and thanked Executive Chairman Lee for making the exhibition possible. Business leaders attending the gala included those from BT Group, Vodafone, Sainsbury’s, and Standard Chartered. From academia, representatives from the University of Oxford and Imperial College London were in attendance, while the cultural sector was represented by the British Museum, Tate Modern, the V&A, and Lisson Gallery, alongside contemporary artist Marc Quinn. Samsung’s business partners from the semiconductor industry, including Christophe Fouquet, CEO of ASML, Kai Beckmann, CEO of Merck, Andreas Pecher, CEO of ZEISS, and Patrick Vandenameele, CEO of imec, were among other notable attendees. Chairman Lee Expresses Gratitude to Korean War Veterans During his remarks, Executive Chairman Lee took a special moment to honor the three Korean War veterans in attendance, including Mike Roe. He also thanked The Princess Royal, recognising her visit to Korea in July 2026 during which she honored the veterans. Reflecting on more than 140 years of ties between Korea and the U.K., he highlighted Samsung’s 80-year business relationship with the country and emphasised that the U.K. has served as the hub for its European operations for over five decades. The London exhibition features 100 masterpieces, including 10 National Treasures and 13 Treasures of Korea, with more than twenty pieces being revealed for the first time internationally. Among the newly presented works are the National Treasures “Bronze Artifacts from Bisan-dong, Daegu” and “Bronze Rattles,” as well as “Celadon Incense Burner with Girin-shaped Lid.” Among the modern and contemporary works, Nam June Paik’s “Brahms,” Lee Jungseop’s “Bound People,” and Park Rehyun’s “Woman” will also be shown for the first time. The Lee family’s commitment to preserving and sharing Korea’s culture spans three generations. It began with Samsung founder Lee Byung-Chull, who built the foundation of the collection and believed that cultural heritage should be passed on to future generations. His son, the late Samsung Chairman Lee Kun-Hee carried this legacy forward, building and preserving the collection over decades. He viewed cultural heritage not simply as something to be owned, but as something to be protected and preserved. Director Emerita Hong Ra-Hee also played a crucial role in expanding and developing the collection to encompass both ancient and modern works. The Lee Kun-Hee Collection, now a national cultural asset, is reaching audiences in major cities around the world from Washington D.C. to Chicago to London, enabling them to experience and appreciate the value and historical significance of Korean culture, thereby elevating Korea’s global standing. The collection’s global tour began in November 2025 at the Smithsonian’s National Museum of Asian Art in Washington D.C., attracting about 80,000 visitors to become the museum’s largest special exhibition in the past 10 years. The collection then traveled to the Art Institute of Chicago, where it drew approximately 115,000 visitors, highlighting the strong interest in the rich history of Korean arts and culture. Samsung remains committed to introducing Korean cultural heritage to the world while continuing to expand its global business network to support future growth and innovation.

title: Samsung Galaxy SmartTag3 Makes It Easier To Keep Track of What Matters
text: Samsung Electronics today announced the new Galaxy SmartTag3, a compact tracker that combines a smaller, lighter design with longer-range finding, cross-OS support, faster location updates through the Galaxy Find Network and expanded proactive alerts. 1 “People want simpler and more convenient ways to keep track of belongings and pets for greater peace of mind, and Galaxy SmartTag3 was designed around those everyday needs,” said Jay Kim, Executive Vice President and Head of Customer Experience Office, Mobile eXperience (MX) Business at Samsung Electronics. “Powered by the vast Galaxy Find Network, it delivers our most capable Galaxy SmartTag experience yet.” Versatile Design, More Possibilities Galaxy SmartTag3 introduces a compact design that is approximately 35% smaller by volume and 33% lighter than the previous generation, 2 making it easier to attach to keys, smaller bags, luggage, or a pet collar. 3 Its rounded form is finished with an aluminum-decorated button for a refined, durable feel, while new official accessories including a Silicone Case with a keyring and a Loop Case offer even more flexibility. 4 For the first time in the Galaxy SmartTag lineup, Galaxy SmartTag3 also brings cross-OS compatibility for Galaxy and iOS devices, making it easier for families and groups to access core finding and sharing features across platforms. Through SmartThings Find, users can check and share a tag’s location and use Search Nearby across supported devices. 5 This is especially useful when a friend or family member borrows a suitcase for a trip, allowing them to check its location and use supported finding features from their own Galaxy or iOS device. Galaxy SmartTag3 offers industry-leading battery life, with up to 550 days under standard usage and up to 790 days in Power Saving Mode. 6 See Further, Find Faster When something goes missing, knowing where to start looking can make all the difference. Galaxy SmartTag3 significantly expands the range of Compass View, 7 helping users begin narrowing in on an item from farther away. Bluetooth 6.0 Channel Sounding enables Compass View to provide distance and directional guidance from up to 60 meters away — around three times farther than the previous generation. As users get closer, ultra-wideband (UWB) delivers even greater precision, creating a more continuous finding experience from long range to close range. If a set of keys goes missing somewhere in a large park, Compass View can help users narrow in on its location from farther away and guide them more precisely as they get closer. When Galaxy SmartTag3 moves beyond direct connection range, the Galaxy Find Network helps keep the search going. More than 900 million participating Galaxy devices worldwide can act as finding nodes, helping detect Galaxy SmartTag3 and update its location beyond the reach of the user’s own phone. 8 Faster Galaxy Find Network updates can surface new location information sooner after disconnection, helping reduce uncertainty when luggage or another tagged belonging is unexpectedly separated from its owner. Stay Informed Proactively Galaxy SmartTag3 goes beyond finding by helping users stay informed without actively searching. The new Place Notification 9 feature adds a proactive layer, letting users define an area and receive an alert when a tagged item moves in or out of it. Using location data from the Galaxy Find Network, Place Notification can notify users when a family pet leaves the garden or when a bicycle is detected moving out of its usual parking area. Instead of requiring users to repeatedly check a location, Galaxy SmartTag3 can surface the information when it becomes relevant. Location History 10 lets users review where their tag has been, while Movement Detection Alert 11 can notify them when movement is detected so they can stay informed without actively checking. 12 Built for Everyday Privacy and Confidence Galaxy SmartTag3 retains an IP67 13 water and dust resistance rating alongside other key Galaxy SmartTag capabilities: NFC-powered Lost Mode, 14 which can display registered contact information or a short message when a lost tag is scanned with a compatible mobile device. SmartThings IoT Control , which allows users to trigger preset routines for compatible connected devices using the tag button. Left Behind Alert , 15 which can notify users when their mobile device loses connection with a tagged belonging. Privacy and security remain central to the Galaxy SmartTag experience with location data that is encrypted to help protect user privacy. Availability Samsung Galaxy SmartTag3 will be available first in Korea beginning Oct. 7, 2026, followed by the U.S., with additional markets to follow in 2027. It will be offered in White and Black. For more information, please visit samsung.com or the Samsung Newsroom. Keep battery and product components out of reach of children and pets. If swallowed, seek immediate medical attention. ︎ Accessories sold separately. Color and availability may vary by carrier and retailer. False alerts may occur if obstacles or environmental factors disrupt the connection, even when the item is still nearby. Feature availability may vary by platform, device and market. title: Samsung Introduces Galaxy Tab S12 Series: The Ultimate Productivity Powerhouse Built for Growth
text: Samsung Electronics today unveiled the Galaxy Tab S12 series — Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and Tab S12+ — delivering Samsung’s most capable and versatile tablet experience yet. Packing breakthrough performance, long-lasting battery life, and the latest Galaxy AI 1 into Galaxy Tab’s signature ultra-thin design, the new lineup turns complex workflows into effortless, everyday achievements whether it’s mastering skills, pursuing career goals, or exploring creative passions. Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and Tab S12+ feature immersive displays and come bundled with the ergonomically designed S Pen for effortless note-taking and precise editing. With easy access to professional-grade apps and versatile accessories, users can pursue their passions and progress toward their goals with ease. Combining portability with professional-grade power, the Galaxy Tab S12 series gives users instant access to powerful capabilities whenever inspiration strikes. “The Galaxy Tab S12 series is designed for people who are constantly exploring new ideas, developing new skills, and bringing their ambitions to life,” said Jay Kim, Executive Vice President and Head of Customer Experience Office, Mobile eXperience (MX) Business at Samsung Electronics. “Built with industry-leading hardware, the Galaxy Tab S12 series pairs an expansive screen with the power of Galaxy AI — removing friction from complex tasks so users can stay focused on achieving impactful results.” Peak Performance in an Ultra-Thin Design The Galaxy Tab S12 series combines powerful performance and long-lasting battery life into a thin and light design, making it easy for users to achieve more, wherever ambition takes them. At a remarkably slim 5.1mm, Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra is Samsung’s thinnest Galaxy Tab, while delivering the most powerful performance of any Galaxy Tab to date, supporting productive use throughout the day. For example, users taking an online course alongside a full-time job can catch up on a lesson during the commute, then work through course exercises on the large screen at a café or library later in the day. prev next Both models are built to go the distance, allowing users to keep going without losing momentum. On a single charge, the all-day battery lasts up to 23 hours on Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra 2 and up to 21 hours on Galaxy Tab S12+, 3 supporting long stretches of productivity anywhere. When it is time to recharge, the battery goes from 0% to 100% in about 95 minutes with the 45W adapter — minimizing downtime so users can get back to what they were doing. 4 Beyond long-lasting battery life, the Galaxy Tab S12 series delivers the most powerful performance of any Galaxy Tab to date, keeping pace with even intensive tasks. The cutting-edge 3nm processor delivers up to 61% faster NPU processing, 19% faster CPU performance, and 17% improved GPU power compared to Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra. 5 In everyday use, that means users can take on more demanding tasks with increased speed and responsiveness. Whether rendering complex creative projects or watching a lecture while taking notes and asking AI for clarification — the experience stays responsive and fast with fewer interruptions to break their focus. A newly designed 3D Vapor Chamber efficiently dissipates heat to support more reliable performance during demanding tasks, whether users are editing video or designing graphics for hours. 6 Engineered for resilience and durability to withstand the elements and give users peace of mind, the Galaxy Tab S12 series also comes with IP68-rated water and dust resistance . 7 The Galaxy Tab S12 series comes with an expansive screen designed to help users think bigger and give ideas more room to unfold. Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra features a large 14.6-inch display, making it easy to explore complex topics and keep multiple perspectives in view. The Galaxy Tab S12+ features a larger 12.6-inch display and slimmer bezels than its predecessor, offering more screen space without sacrificing portability. Both models feature Dynamic AMOLED 2X displays reaching up to 1,600 nits of peak brightness 8 — delivering clear, vivid visuals indoors, or out. The upgraded seamless Vision Booster now adjusts brightness in real time based on lighting conditions for comfortable viewing. Sound gets a major upgrade as well, with 4-channel spatial audio — twice as many channels as the previous generation — delivering a richer, more immersive experience whether users are streaming content, following a tutorial, or editing. Making Everyday Tasks More Intuitive and Effortless Building on an industry-leading hardware foundation, the Galaxy Tab S12 series turns its large screen into a flexible workspace that makes it easy to keep up with different tasks without missing a beat. Running Android 17 with One UI 9 and the latest Galaxy AI , it brings research, note-taking, creation, and AI assistance into one place, giving users more freedom to explore new ideas, capture what matters and put what they learn into practice. Thanks to the Galaxy Tab S12 series’ immersive screen, users can split the screen into up to three sections in Multi Window layout. For example, users can take notes in Samsung Notes on one side while playing a lecture and opening an AI assistant on the other. As key takeaways or questions come up, users can capture them with the S Pen directly in Samsung Notes, while Note Assist 9 summarizes their notes 10 – all without pausing the lecture. prev next Both models come bundled with an ergonomic S Pen, offering precise, intuitive input for note-taking, annotating materials, and sketching concepts. For a more structured, professional workstation, the Pro Keyboard elevates productivity with a premium aluminum finish and a Galaxy AI Key that enables instant access to AI assistants, while the Book Cover Keyboard Slim delivers flexibility with comfortable viewing angles and an effortless typing experience. 11 prev next The Galaxy Tab S12 series helps users bring information together and get real-time support the moment curiosity strikes. The Galaxy Tab S12 series comes equipped with a six-month trial of Google AI Pro , 12 providing expanded access to Google’s most capable AI models from day one. Users can ask Gemini about anything unclear or dive deeper into subjects they want to explore the moment a question comes up. With Gemini Notebook , users can bring together notes, images, recordings, and files in one workspace and create summaries, podcasts, and even quizzes to make key information easier to understand. As exploration expands into deeper research, Samsung Browser helps users stay focused without losing track of what they have already discovered. By understanding webpage content, context across multiple tabs, and browsing history, it can summarize information across open pages or surface a relevant source viewed days earlier – helping users spend less time searching through past tabs and more time capturing the key insights that matter most. 13 prev next A Complete Ecosystem Designed To Take Skills and Creativity Further The Galaxy Tab S12 series gives users the ideal place to put knowledge into practice, bringing together professional-grade apps 14 alongside benefits worth approximately $600 15 to help them take their skills further. Adobe Photoshop 16 comes pre-loaded on the Galaxy Tab S12 series — a first for Android tablets — bringing pro-grade image editing and design to the tablet. The interface is optimized for tablets, and S Pen support makes it more intuitive to move ideas from hand to screen. Photoshop includes AI-powered features including AI Assistant 17 and generative AI features powered by Adobe Firefly like Generative Fill and Image to Video, helping creatives edit faster and effortlessly. Exclusively for the Galaxy Tab S12 series, users receive four months of free access to the Photoshop mobile plan. Notability , 18 newly pre-loaded on Galaxy Tab, helps users capture their ideas, organize notes, and build knowledge more efficiently with S Pen optimization and AI-driven study tools with a six-month free trial, plus 20% off the first subscription. Goodnotes 19 delivers clean note-taking and organization with one year of free access and LumaFusion 20 enables professional-grade video editing, offered at a 66% discount. And Notion 21 supports flexible writing, planning, and organization with one month of its Plus plan free. Clip Studio Paint 22 brings precision drawing and painting tools for digital art with a six-month trial and 20% off the first subscription. In addition to these apps, users can explore a broader range of options that support different needs. MyScript Math instantly solves handwritten equations and shows the steps behind each one, while MyScript Notes summarizes handwritten notes into study materials with built-in AI tools to explain concepts or generate quizzes. Noteshelf 3 23 offers customizable layouts for capturing and organizing ideas, while ArcSite 24 converts rough field sketches into precise CAD drawings. Availability The Galaxy Tab S12 series will be available starting Oct. 7 in select markets and offered in two colors, Gray and Silver. 25 Built for lasting and confident use, Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and Galaxy Tab S12+ support up to seven times of OS upgrades and security updates. 26 For added peace of mind, Samsung Care+ 27 offers comprehensive coverage tailored to users’ device needs, including fast repairs for accidental damage, extended warranty, and certified expert support available both at home and abroad. Additionally, Galaxy mobile phone users running One UI 9 can easily check the Samsung Care+ status of their Galaxy Tab and enroll through the Warranty and care menu in the Settings. It provides quick access to warranty information, self-diagnostics, repair requests, and remote support for connected devices—all directly from the mobile phone. For additional information, visit Samsung Newsroom , SamsungMobilePress.com , or Samsung.com . title: Samsung To Invest USD 1 Billion in AI Infrastructure Company Helix
text: Samsung Electronics, Samsung C&T, Samsung SDS, Samsung SDI, Samsung Life Insurance and Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance today announced they are investing a combined USD 1 billion in Helix Digital Infrastructure, an AI infrastructure company established by global investment firm KKR. Launched in June 2026, Helix is an AI-enabling infrastructure provider that is designed to deliver integrated solutions across the entire value chain, including hyperscale data center development and operations, power generation (covering both baseload and flexible energy sources), transmission and distribution infrastructure, and fiber-optic networks. Through Helix, hyperscalers can rapidly secure the large-scale, comprehensive infrastructure required to keep pace with exponentially growing AI demands. Helix is led by Adam Selipsky, former CEO of Amazon Web Services (AWS) and is assembling a dedicated management team comprising leading experts from the data center and power industries. Helix also leverages the capabilities of KKR’s leading global infrastructure business with about 170 dedicated professionals. Alongside Samsung, KKR, the Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA), NVIDIA, and US power company Vistra are also founding investors in Helix. AI Data Centers Evolve Into Core Platforms for a New Industrial Ecosystem AI data centers are rapidly evolving beyond simple facility investments into core business platforms. Today, they integrate diverse, high-value business models, including GPU-as-a-Service (GPUaaS), Sovereign AI, and colocation services. The rapid expansion of these data centers is driving the creation of a massive, multi-sector ecosystem that spans power generation, cooling technologies, semiconductors, and finance. Samsung affiliates’ investment reflects a strategic commitment to securing next-generation AI leadership within this emerging infrastructure landscape. As AI services integrate deeper into daily life and global industries, the need for data centers capable of processing massive compute workloads — and the specialized power infrastructure required to run them stably — is growing exponentially. If data centers are the production hubs of the AI era, power is the fuel that drives them. Consequently, the ability to secure both compute and power infrastructure simultaneously has emerged as a defining competitive advantage in the AI industry. By targeting both data center deployment and the underlying power infrastructure, Helix’s investment strategy addresses the very core of this market competition. Recognizing that power availability is currently the greatest bottleneck in AI infrastructure, Helix plans to rapidly secure energy capacity through direct investments and strategic partnerships with major energy developers, including investor Vistra. The investment this time is expected to serve as a pivotal milestone for Samsung’s affiliates, allowing them to leverage their world-class hardware and component expertise to build system- and infrastructure-level influence. Moving forward, Samsung is poised to expand its role from a traditional hardware component supplier to an active architect of the global AI infrastructure ecosystem. Samsung’s Expertise Across the AI Infrastructure Stack Serves as Critical Anchor for Global AI Buildout Samsung Electronics’ Device Solutions (DS) Division supports the global buildout with its state-of-the-art semiconductor solutions, responding to changes in global demand in a timely manner. Samsung Electronics’ Device eXperience (DX) Division delivers a comprehensive portfolio of data center cooling products and solutions — from air cooling systems to coolant distribution units (CDUs) for liquid cooling — through FläktGroup, its data center HVAC specialist subsidiary acquired in 2025. It also operates 14 production sites worldwide and a supply and service network across 65 countries, giving it the speed and flexibility to meet hyperscalers’ demands for rapid capacity expansion. Samsung C&T Engineering & Construction Group is actively driving the large-scale infrastructure projects as an engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contractor across data centers and power generation. Samsung SDS is an IT solutions provider that also designs, builds and operates data centers and has recently ventured into the GPUaaS business. The company boasts the lowest power usage effectiveness (PUE) level in Korea which it applies both to its own data centers and to the Korea AI Computing Center (KOACC). Samsung SDI is recognized for world-leading technology in uninterruptible power supplies (UPS) and battery backup units (BBUs), both essential to running data centers that operate high-performance servers 24 hours a day. It plans to explore new business opportunities in this field, where ultra-high-output, high-capacity battery technology is essential. Through this investment, Samsung Electronics and its affiliates aim to accelerate global AI data center deployment alongside Helix, while maximizing collaborative synergies among participating companies.

title: [World Heart Day] Taking Care of Your Heart Every Day, Starting From Your Wrist
text: No matter who you are or what you do, we all have one constant companion we rely on every single day: our heart. Unseen but always at work, it beats around 100,000 times a day, keeping pace with us through every moment. Yet for something so essential to our lives, taking care of our hearts is often overlooked until it’s too late. Heart disease is the number one cause of death worldwide, 1 which is why the World Health Organization (WHO) and the World Heart Federation recognize Sept. 29 as World Heart Day . It is a reminder that the choices we make today can make a meaningful difference tomorrow. These choices don’t have to be big. From choosing when to go to bed to making time for even just 30 minutes of exercise, the small choices we make every day add up to a healthier lifestyle. The good news is that Samsung Galaxy Watch can help you make proactive prevention part of daily life. By monitoring your sleep, activity level, stress, and blood pressure, Galaxy Watch helps you better understand what’s happening in your body and what steps to take to ensure your heart is doing its job well. Understanding Your Body at a Glance: Heart Health Score The American Heart Association recommends looking at Life’s Essential 8 2 as key measures for improving and maintaining cardiovascular health: diet, exercise, sleep, weight, blood pressure, blood sugar, cholesterol and smoking cessation. But knowing what matters raises an important question: how do these factors change the choices we make every day? Samsung Health’s Heart Health Score is designed to help you in this journey. It tracks and analyzes complex health indicators such as sleep duration, daily activity level, body composition and vascular load, 3 converting them into a single, simple score that anyone can intuitively understand and follow. Think about what happens if you miss your daily exercise for a few days: your Galaxy Watch recognizes your moderate-to-high intensity activity level has decreased, reflects this change in a lower Heart Health Score, and makes a recommendation to go for a run. With convenient insights right from your wrist, Galaxy Watch delivers personalized insights that make it easier to recognize changes, understand your habits, and take the next step toward healthier ones. prev next ▲ Galaxy Watch and Samsung Health provide effortless understanding of cardiovascular wellness through the Heart Health Score (Image simulated for illustrative purposes. Actual UX/UI may differ.) Advanced Sensor Technology: From Measurement to Meaning Samsung Galaxy Watches are equipped with an advanced BioActive Sensor which integrates three precision sensors in one: an optical heart rate sensor (PPG), an electrocardiogram sensor (ECG), 4 and a bioelectrical impedance analysis sensor (BIA). With calibration just once every four weeks using a home blood pressure monitor, you can easily check your blood pressure 5 from your wrist anytime, anywhere. When you place your finger on the watch’s side electrode for just 30 seconds, the watch measures an electrocardiogram to detect signs of abnormal heartbeats like atrial fibrillation or ectopic beats. The Irregular Heart Rhythm Notification (IHRN) 6 feature, which detects abnormal heart signals, monitors the user’s heart rhythm throughout the day and provides a proactive notification if abnormal signs are repeated. Even small reminders like this have the power to save lives. In several countries, these notifications have led to early detection of risks such as atherosclerosis or myocardial infarction. ▲ Galaxy Watch supports heart rhythm monitoring through irregular heart rhythm notifications and ECG readings. (Image simulated for illustrative purposes. Actual UX/UI may differ.) Around-the-Clock Care: How Galaxy Watch Proactively Monitors Your Health Even During Sleep Your heart is a constant you can count on, and it works whether you’re awake or asleep. When you wear your Galaxy Watch to sleep, it analyzes five major vital signs: heart rate during sleep, heart rate variability, 7 respiratory rate, skin temperature, and blood oxygen saturation. These signals are compared against your personal baseline. When you wake up, your Galaxy Watch will send a notification if it detects meaningful deviations from your baseline. By highlighting meaningful changes early, it gives you an opportunity to rest, recover or seek medical guidance before small issues become larger concerns. 8 ▲ Galaxy Watch and Samsung Health give users a clear view of their sleep quality with detailed metrics and insights they can use to improve their sleep habits. (Image simulated for illustrative purposes. Actual UX/UI may differ.) Heart to Heart: Connected Care That Adds Peace of Mind Looking after your own heart is only one side of the story. From parents to partners, siblings to grandparents or even friends, the burden of caring for the hearts of those around you weighs heavily. Samsung Health’s Health Data Sharing 9 function lightens the load by sharing agreed-upon data items (number of steps, blood pressure, heart rate, medication adherence, etc.) with loved ones. You can check if your parents who live far away have completed their daily walk or taken their prescribed medication on time, just as if you were right there with them. ▲ Samsung Health lets users share selected health data with loved ones, helping them stay connected and informed about one another’s wellbeing. (Image simulated for illustrative purposes. Actual UX/UI may differ.) World Heart Day coincides with the seasonal transition when chilly winds begin to blow in the mornings and evenings. As the temperature gap between day and night widens, blood vessels constrict, sharply increasing the risk of cardiovascular disease. The key to preventing heart disease lies not in reactive treatment, but in proactive habits of paying close attention to the subtle signals your body sends every day. Start managing your heart health with Galaxy Watch, a reliable health partner that stays with you around the clock. It continuously analyzes changes during sleep to provide a comprehensive score. ︎ Electrocardiogram (ECG) feature records and analyzes subtle electrical signals of the heart when the user places a finger on Galaxy Watch’s top button for about 30 seconds, detecting atrial fibrillation (irregular and rapid quivering) and ectopic beats (premature irregular beats). ︎ Blood Pressure feature measures systolic and diastolic blood pressure by analyzing pulse waveforms with Galaxy Watch’s optical (PPG) sensor. An initial measurement using a separate cuff-type blood pressure monitor is required, and recalibration is needed every 4 weeks (28 days). ︎ Irregular Heart Rhythm Notification (IHRN) feature detects irregular patterns that may indicate atrial fibrillation through pulse monitoring and provides an early alert. ︎ Heart Rate Variability (HRV) feature analyzes minute-to-minute variations in the intervals between heartbeats to show autonomic nervous system balance. title: Samsung Art Store Debuts First-Ever Cinematic Collection for Samsung TVs
text: Samsung Art Store 1 has announced its first-ever cinematic collection, featuring 38 stills from acclaimed films produced by studio A24. Available on supported Samsung Art TVs worldwide, the collection allows subscribers to revisit memorable moments and discover new favorites at home. ▲ A still from “Midsommar,” courtesy of A24 A24 is a global entertainment company that produces and distributes films, TV series, documentaries, music, and consumer products. title: Samsung TV Plus Expands Global Creator Lineup to More Markets
text: Samsung TV Plus is expanding its creator offerings to more markets worldwide. Samsung Electronics’ subscription-free streaming service introduced new creator-led channels across Australia, New Zealand, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and the United Kingdom — while extending existing creator channels to Brazil and Mexico. Spanning lifestyle, food, sports, news, and science, the additions broaden access to content from leading creators. The new global offerings include: U.K.: In partnership with 208 Studios, Samsung TV Plus has launched three new creator channels. Happy Place: Interviews from the acclaimed podcast by Fearne Cotton, who has more than 15 million social media followers. Golf Life: Golf and comedy from Ange, Jimmy, and Tubes Bullard, who have more than 3 million combined followers JOE Media: News and entertainment from the U.K. media brand, which has more than 30 million followers across platforms. Australia, New Zealand, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand: Luke Nguyen’s World follows Australian-Vietnamese chef, restaurateur and television personality Luke Nguyen as he explores food, culture, and travel. The program features more than 95 episodes across nine seasons, adding to Nguyen’s portfolio of content aired in more than 150 countries. Brazil & Mexico: Mark Rober TV is now available in these markets. It is a dedicated 24-hour science and engineering channel featuring dubbed content from former NASA engineer Mark Rober, who has more than 79 million followers across platforms. title: Samsung, SK Telecom, and Hana Financial Group Build Korea’s First Private 5G Smart Office in the Financial Sector
text: Samsung Electronics today announced that the company serves as the sole vendor to deliver its private 5G network solutions, powering a smart office at Hana Financial Group’s new headquarters in Incheon, South Korea. As the first of its kind in the Korean financial sector, this new connected office elevates convenience in mobility and provides a foundation for enterprise AI transformation (AX) while meeting the stringent security requirements of this industry. In collaboration with SK Telecom and Samsung, Hana Financial Group built out a large-scale smart office, spanning 16 floors of its headquarters, multiple group affiliates, and thousands of employees. Using 5G-enabled laptops, tablets, and mobile devices, employees can access a seamless work environment anytime, anywhere. This enhanced connectivity drives more efficient use of office space, supports employee productivity, and fosters a more agile way of working, while reducing the time and resources needed to reconfigure the building. It also lays the groundwork for adopting AI across daily operations. Financial institutions handle highly sensitive data such as customers’ credit and bank information, and operate under strict network-separation requirements — leaving Wi-Fi adoption largely off-limits over security concerns and cyber risks. This project deploys a multi-layered security system, encompassing enhanced encryption, a firewall, DDoS protection, and USIM-based authentication — granting network access exclusively to authorized devices and registered users. Samsung’s private 5G solutions offer both the complete isolation of wired networks and the convenience of wireless connectivity. “For AI and data to be used widely in day-to-day work, employees need a network that gives them secure, reliable access to internal systems and data from anywhere,” said Kim Goo-Young, Head of Enterprise Business Office at SK Telecom. “Built on Samsung’s core and radio solutions, that secure foundation is now in place — making this smart office a leading example of how we innovate the way the financial sector works.” For this project, Samsung provided its full stack of network solutions including radios, baseband, and cloud-native core, supporting the mid-band (4.7GHz) spectrum dedicated to private 5G networks in Korea. Samsung’s 5G Standalone Core enables network slicing, which divides a single physical network infrastructure into multiple virtual slices where each is dedicated to a specific application. Through this deployment, Hana Financial Group’s subsidiaries will each have access to separate network slices, offering independent operating environments tailored to individual security policies and business needs. “This meaningful milestone underscores Samsung’s leadership in deploying private 5G solutions that deliver even under the most stringent security standards required by regulated industries,” said Angelo Jeongho Park, Executive Vice President and Head of Strategic Sales, Networks Business at Samsung Electronics. “By combining cutting-edge technology and our extensive commercial experiences across diverse industries — including manufacturing, finance, construction, IT, and more — we are providing secure, tailored networks today while enabling businesses to seamlessly integrate AI-driven innovations.” Samsung Networks has pioneered the successful delivery of 5G end-to-end solutions, including chipsets, radios, and cores. Through ongoing research and development, Samsung is driving the industry to advance 5G networks and paving the way for 6G and beyond with its market-leading product portfolio, from purpose-built RAN, vRAN, Open RAN, AI RAN, and cloud-native AI core to private network solutions and AI-powered automation tools (CognitiV NOS). The company currently provides innovative network solutions to mobile operators that deliver boundless connectivity to hundreds of millions of users worldwide.

title: Samsung at the Forefront of Korea’s AI RAN Projects with KT and SK Telecom
text: Samsung Electronics today announced it has signed contracts with KT and SK Telecom for their AI RAN projects under the Korean Ministry of Science and ICT’s (MSIT) “Hyper AI Network” initiative, taking on the roles of sole global vendor for KT and main vendor for SK Telecom. Building on its decades-long partnerships with the country’s leading operators and its leadership in software-driven, AI-native network innovation, Samsung is the only partner selected for both projects. Set to begin in October 2026, the projects will deploy 5G Standalone (SA) private networks across industrial environments, ranging from shipyards to petrochemical facilities, to validate AI RAN capabilities and generate real-world insights for future deployments. As part of the Korean MSIT’s initiative, the projects bring together operators, network solution providers, and other industry partners. The collaboration aims to accelerate the adoption of cutting-edge technologies, including AI RAN, physical AI, and autonomous operations, while laying the groundwork for the transition to 6G. “Korea has long stood at the forefront of global digital and technological advancement. As a key partner with deep roots in this region, we are proud to drive the next stage of network innovation alongside leading operators through these AI RAN projects,” said June Moon, Executive Vice President, Head of R&D, Networks Business at Samsung Electronics. “As AI evolves toward embodied intelligence, networks are becoming platforms that connect a new generation of intelligent machines, including humanoids and autonomous vehicles. Bringing AI RAN and physical AI together in real-world industrial settings marks a meaningful step toward the future of connectivity.” AI-Powered Welding Robots at Shipyards At the Yeongam Shipyard of HD Hyundai Samho, a prominent global shipbuilder, KT will carry out field trials of key physical AI services, ranging from welding and painting robots in manufacturing environments to autonomous robots for telecom facility operations. For the AI-powered quadruped welding robot use case, Samsung will support KT with its software-driven, AI-native solutions, including Network in a Server (NIS) — an integrated edge AI platform comprising virtualized RAN (vRAN), AI Core, and AI applications — and Samsung CognitiV Network Operations Suite (NOS) for intelligent network automation. Leveraging 5G connectivity and the edge AI platform, the quadruped robot can autonomously perceive its working environment and perform precise welding. With these capabilities, Samsung is addressing the demanding network requirements of physical AI services in industrial settings, where ultra-low latency, high reliability, and consistent throughput are critical for real-time robotic control. Designed for on-premise deployment and local processing, NIS brings network and AI capabilities closer to where data is generated and decisions are made. It runs vRAN and 5G SA core software on an AMD EPYC 8004 Server CPU-powered commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) Compact Edge Server from Supermicro with Wind River Cloud Platform. Its software-driven architecture also enables flexible scaling, with the ability to incorporate accelerated GPU compute as needed to meet site-specific requirements. “KT views this project as an important starting point for validating the next-generation communications paradigm where AI and networks converge,” said Jongsik Lee, Executive Vice President, KT. “Together with Samsung, we will demonstrate a range of Physical AI services in an AI-RAN-enabled private network environment and secure the key technologies and service models that will lead the AI-Native 6G era.” Autonomous Patrol Robots at Petrochemical Facilities As another key part of the country’s Hyper AI Network initiative, SK Telecom will validate physical AI services at SK Incheon Petrochem, a major energy hub for the Seoul metropolitan area. These capabilities include an autonomous robot that patrols hazardous areas and CCTV-based monitoring. The patrol robot transfers high-definition videos in real time while on the move, enabling AI analysis to detect potential hazards and facilitate integrated monitoring. Samsung is providing its AI-native NIS solution for SK Telecom’s project. The companies will explore how AI-native connectivity can further enhance safety and efficiency in petrochemical environments, where complex chemical processes require rigorous monitoring and operational precision. “At SK Telecom, we believe AI creates greater value when paired with the right foundation to support it, and this project puts that belief into practice,” said Takki Yu, Head of Network Technology Office at SK Telecom. “Drawing on our AI expertise, we will work with Samsung to validate physical AI services in real-world environments and advance AI RAN as a key technology underpinning the government’s Hyper AI Network initiative and its AI Highway agenda.” Samsung’s AI RAN delivers a range of capabilities, including anomaly detection, throughput enhancement, and energy efficiency improvements, all validated on live networks around the globe. Building on this experience, Samsung continues to work with leading operators and partners to expand the real-world footprint of AI-native, 6G-ready networks and propel the adoption of AI-driven services across global markets. Samsung Networks has pioneered the successful delivery of 5G end-to-end solutions, including chipsets, radios, and cores. Through ongoing research and development, Samsung is driving the industry to advance 5G networks and paving the way for 6G and beyond with its market-leading product portfolio, from purpose-built RAN, vRAN, Open RAN, AI RAN, and cloud-native AI core to private network solutions and AI-powered automation tools (CognitiV NOS). The company currently provides innovative network solutions to mobile operators that deliver boundless connectivity to hundreds of millions of users worldwide.

title: Bringing Fantasy Characters to Life: Samsung Spatial Signage Transforms Tokyo Game Show 2026
text: At Tokyo Game Show (TGS) 2026, held from September 17 to 20 at Makuhari Messe in Chiba, Japan, Samsung Electronics and NC demonstrated the future of fan engagement by bringing the characters of Astrae Oratio — the upcoming urban fantasy RPG — into the physical world through glasses-free 3D Spatial Signage. The installation transformed a conventional booth into an immersive experience where visitors encountered lifelike characters at scale, blurring the line between digital worlds and physical spaces. Extending Fan Engagement Into Physical Spaces For game publishers and IP owners, the challenge lies in translating digital characters into physical environments. At the entrance to the booth of NC, a global game developer and publishing company, an 85-inch Spatial Signage display was integrated into an elevator-themed installation and introduced Astrae Oratio characters at near life-size scale. Featuring Samsung’s patented 3D Plate technology, Spatial Signage created a vivid sense of depth without requiring viewers to wear 3D glasses, bringing the game’s characters and its magical world into the physical space. “We wanted visitors to come face-to-face with the characters at life-size scale and feel immersed in the game’s world from the moment they entered the booth,” said Yongsoo Lee, Head of Astrae Oratio Business Division at NC. “For games in the subculture genre, the liveliness and realism of the characters are especially important. We believed that Samsung Spatial Signage would make this possible.” ▲ The 85-inch Spatial Signage created the impression that characters from Astrae Oratio are stepping out of an elevator into the real world. Visitors responded immediately to the display’s scale, movement, and sense of depth. Content creator Kawaii CoCo noted, “The character felt interactive because she was moving around, which made her feel a little more human-like. That really caught my attention.” She added that the display’s social media presence was undeniable. “It’s much more prominent and looks much better on social media, so I wanted to capture some footage and show my audience this really cool display.” ▲ Content creator Kawaii CoCo emphasized how the character’s lifelike movement made the display feel interactive and eye-catching for social media. Despite its slim 52mm profile, 1 Spatial Signage is designed to create the visual impression of depth, making it appear as though the space extends behind the screen. This immersive effect creates a powerful impression when viewers first encounter a game and its characters in public settings. Booth visitor Daniel Acero said, “Having this as the first impression of the game in public is really helpful for shaping public perception of the game. It also conveys the personalities of the characters.” He added, “I didn’t realize it was a display screen. I thought it was a transparent screen with an actual space behind it. It really created a strong sense of depth.” Beyond the entrance, compact 32-inch Spatial Signage displays, with an even slimmer profile of 49.4mm, were placed in waiting areas and along the visitor route, extending the character experience throughout the booth. The smaller form factor enabled flexible installation in space-constrained areas while helping visitors remain engaged with the game’s characters and its world as they waited. Visitor Tomas Portier said, “Even if the queue was kind of long, Spatial Signage helped the time pass more quickly while helping me get to know the characters a little better. It’s more lively than a still image or a conventional screen.” ▲ A compact 32-inch Spatial Signage display presented an Astrae Oratio character in the booth’s waiting area, extending the experience along the visitor route. Creating Visual Impact While Maximizing Space For retailers and venue operators, visual impact needs to work within the realities of physical space. Spatial Signage’s slim profile, combined with glasses-free 3D presentation, enabled NC to make strategic use of limited space. “Designing the visitor flow was quite challenging, but since Spatial Signage is very slim, it was really easy to install and make effective use of the space,” Yongsoo Lee explained. “That also gave us room to store merchandise for visitors.” ▲ Yongsoo Lee, Head of Astrae Oratio Business Division at NC. At the booth entrance, NC used the installation as both a visual focal point and a functional part of the layout. While the display captured visitors’ attention, the area behind it provided concealed storage for merchandise. Visitor David Yousefi observed, “When you present it like this in a box, I thought it was much larger.” He added, “But it’s pretty cool that you can put it all into such a limited space.” ▲ (From left) David Yousefi and Nicolas Felix experienced the striking depth of an Astrae Oratio character, delivered through Spatial Signage’s slim, space-saving design. This flexibility could help character IP owners, retailers, and venue operators bring content into a wider range of physical environments. Miguel Moren, a gaming industry professional and TGS 2026 exhibitor, said, “Having animated video game characters in a real-life space creates a really nice blend of the imaginary world and the real world.” Visitors expressed enthusiasm about potential applications beyond gaming events. Rio Matsushita suggested, “I think having your favorite character move right in front of you is a really great experience. Even while waiting, I could clearly see the three-dimensional visuals. I think it would be a lot of fun if we could see something like that in places like Akihabara too.” Nicolas Felix also saw other opportunities for Spatial Signage. “I think it could be used for commercial branding in shops, for example, to showcase clothes on people,” he said. Yousefi also pointed to additional applications in other public-facing environments. “I could also see it being successful in theme parks or other events where you want to showcase something.” ▲ Visitor Rio Matsushita took photos of the characters appearing on Spatial Signage while waiting in line to play the game. Beyond Tokyo Game Show: Expanding the Possibilities of Spatial Signage The Tokyo Game Show installation is one of several commercial deployments of Samsung Spatial Signage across entertainment, retail, and event environments. At Everland Safari World in Korea , it was integrated into the attraction’s waiting queue, extending the safari experience into areas traditionally reserved for crowd management. The Governors Ball Music Festival in the United States showcased merchandise on an 85-inch display, integrating commerce into the live-event experience. These installations demonstrate how Spatial Signage brings digital content to physical space through a combination of visual impact, spatial efficiency, and visitor engagement. title: Samsung Begins Official Rollout of One UI 9, Bringing the Latest Galaxy Experiences to More Devices
text: Samsung Electronics today announced the expansion of One UI 9 to more Galaxy devices, with the rollout beginning today starting with the Galaxy S26, S26+, and S26 Ultra. 1 Following its debut on Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Fold8, and Flip8, One UI 9 brings an easier, more seamless mobile experience across form factors, as well as enhanced Galaxy AI that is richer, more personal, and more helpful. New Features Help Users Capture, Personalize, and Manage One UI 9 introduces new ways to keep people in focus, tailor the information users see each day, and manage device care more easily. My FanCam 2 automatically tracks a selected person in a recorded video and keeps them centered, intelligently reframing the footage as the scene moves. This allows users to turn dynamic moments into social-ready content with less manual editing. Whether it’s a child’s performance, a friend on the dance floor, or an exciting moment during a sporting event, users can instantly put the focus on the person they want to see. The new Generative and Editable Cards on Now Brief 3 help users choose what appears in their daily summaries. Users can create cards across health, weather, and video so their daily brief reflects the information most relevant to them. Warranty and Care 4 brings device support and protection directly into the Settings menu. Users can now check warranty coverage across connected mobile devices, run self-diagnostics, view repair estimates, and manage Samsung Care+ or book a service appointment with just a few taps. Enhanced Capabilities Help Users Do More With Less Effort One UI 9 builds on familiar Galaxy experiences to help users complete everyday tasks in fewer steps, with context-aware suggestions, timely creative prompts, and improvements to translation, scanning, and recording. Now Nudge 5 can surface timely, context-aware suggestions across more moments in the Galaxy experience, helping users take the next step without breaking their flow. For example, when making plans over text, users can pull up reservation details or save a shared location without leaving the conversation. Creative Studio now suggests image-generation ideas based on relevant upcoming events. For example, when a friend’s birthday is approaching, users may see a prompt to create a themed image or greeting, allowing them to quickly create something meaningful for the occasion. Interpreter 6 introduces a new Thread View that enables users to better follow translated conversations by quickly referencing earlier exchanges. In addition, faster translation in Conversation Mode and quicker playback with compatible Galaxy Buds help reduce delays, making conversations feel more natural and continuous. Document Scan now allows users to digitize challenging materials such as curved book pages and corner-folded papers with less manual adjustment. The large-screen-optimized views on compatible Galaxy devices, along with an improved Finger Eraser, help create cleaner and more usable scans. Voice Recorder presents summaries in a clearer, more structured format, using elements such as headings and tables to make key information easier to scan at a glance. Enhanced Security and Privacy Help Users Stay Informed and in Control One UI 9 continues Samsung’s approach to security and privacy with transparency, choice, and control built into the experience. The latest updates help users better understand when something may need their attention and make it easier to take action. Security Brief brings key security and privacy updates like alerts for malware, apps from unknown sources, and unnecessary permissions to Now Brief, helping users identify potential issues earlier and determine when action is necessary. Privacy Alerts 7 use on-device AI to identify potential privacy risks, including unnecessary attempts to access permissions in the background, giving users greater awareness of how their information is being accessed. Scam Detection 8 expands to additional countries 9 and languages, bringing protection against potential scam calls to more Galaxy users across supported markets. As of the publication of this press release, the official One UI 9 has been rolled out to Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Galaxy Z Fold8, and Galaxy Z Flip8. title: [Interview] The People Behind the Galaxy Z Series’ Camera Innovations ②: How Portrait Video Recreates the Look of Professional Camera Lenses
text: Unveiled at Galaxy Unpacked July 2026, Samsung Electronics’ Galaxy Z series introduces My FanCam — a new feature that lets users focus their edits on a person of their choice — as well as an enhanced Portrait Video that recreates the look of professional camera lenses. While the two features offer different camera experiences, both draw on expertise spanning foundational technology research, feature development, and user experience design. As part of “The People Behind the Galaxy Z Series’ Camera Innovations,” Samsung Newsroom sat down with experts from Samsung Research and the Mobile eXperience (MX) Business to discuss the technical challenges and collaboration behind the two features. A sharply defined subject against a softly blurred background creates a sense of depth long associated with professional camera lenses. Researchers have continued to explore ways to achieve this effect in smartphone video. With the Galaxy Z series, Portrait Video recreates the distinctive depth and Bokeh 1 of a large-aperture lens. 2 To make this possible, Samsung Research analyzed the optical characteristics of actual camera lenses and developed AI-powered video processing technology, while the MX Business optimized it for the device. ▲ (From left) Sang-uk Park, responsible for camera development at the Mobile eXperience (MX) Business, and YoungGeol Kim of the Visual Technology Team at Samsung Research Samsung Newsroom spoke with YoungGeol Kim of the Visual Technology Team at Samsung Research and Sang-uk Park, responsible for camera development at the Mobile eXperience (MX) Business, about how Portrait Video evolved from a research concept into a Galaxy camera feature. A New Level of Depth in Portrait Video Q. What is Portrait Video? What has changed with the latest Galaxy Z series? Park: Portrait Video keeps the main subject in focus while softly blurring the background, creating a cinematic look that makes the subject stand out. ▲ Users can open the Camera app and tap “More” to access Portrait Video. On the Galaxy Z series, the degree of blur changes naturally based on the distance between the subject and background. Small background lights appear as soft, rounded Bokeh, much as they would through a large-aperture lens. This allows users to draw attention to the subject and capture videos with greater depth and atmosphere using just a smartphone, without the need for separate professional equipment. ▲ Comparison of videos with and without Portrait Video on the Galaxy Z series Users can also shift the focus to a different subject or adjust the blur level after filming. ▲ Users can change the subject in focus and adjust the blur level from 0 to 7. Q. What inspired the technology behind Portrait Video? Kim: Photography has been my hobby for 25 years. That passion led me to camera technology research and development and sparked a lasting interest in the unique visual character of lenses. As smartphone cameras advanced rapidly, photography benefited from a range of new features and improvements in image quality. Video evolved quickly as well, but I saw further potential in recreating the depth and background rendering of professional camera lenses. We proposed the idea during the research stage, just as the MX Business was exploring ways to help users create professional-looking videos more easily — paving the way for joint development. ▲ Kim shares the inspiration behind Portrait Video. Q. How did the teams collaborate to turn Portrait Video into a camera feature? Kim: Existing solutions alone weren’t enough to achieve the natural lens rendering we wanted. At the time, Samsung Research’s technology was still in the research stage, so applying it to a product was not an easy decision. Even so, the MX Business recognized its potential and decided to commercialize it. From there, full-scale testing and refinement began. We evaluated the technology on actual devices and exchanged feedback, turning it into a camera feature for users. Park: To prepare the feature for real-world use, we had to shoot countless videos under a wide range of conditions and validate the results. Since the feature is centered on people, experts from both teams even served as models and filmed one another. We focused particularly on how naturally subjects were separated from their backgrounds and whether the blur and Bokeh looked right at different distances. As we filmed each other, reviewed the results together and continued our discussions, what I remember most is how noticeably the results improved. ▲ Park describes the collaboration between the teams. Large-Aperture Lens Rendering on Smartphones Q. What is the key technology that takes Portrait Video to the next level? Kim: The key is technology that recreates the distinctive look of large-aperture professional camera lenses in smartphone video. We used AI and optical analysis to make this possible. Simply blurring an image is not enough to reproduce the depth and natural background rendering of a professional camera. Conventional blur softens an image by blending surrounding colors, but a large-aperture lens works differently. The degree of blur changes naturally based on the distance between the subject and background, while bright points of light spread into Bokeh that retain their shape and brightness. The shapes and textures of these out-of-focus areas are known as bokeh. This requires accounting for both subject-to-background distance and how light spreads through an actual camera lens. ▲ Bokeh captured with Portrait Video on Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra Recreating this effect on a smartphone required two elements. First, we analyzed how light spreads through a real large-aperture lens and the resulting bokeh characteristics, then converted the results into data. We combined this with AI-estimated distance information for the scene, allowing the system to adjust the degree of blur and bokeh size based on the distance between the subject and background. ▲ Process for recreating the effect of a large-aperture lens Q. What technical challenges did the teams face when creating blur and bokeh on smartphones? Kim: The biggest challenge was naturally rendering complex boundaries between the subject and background, such as hair or eyeglass frames. On smartphones, AI-estimated distance information alone isn’t sufficient to accurately distinguish fine boundaries. Even a small error can blur strands of hair or leave parts of the background sharp, making the subject look unnaturally cut out. To address this, we combined AI-estimated distance information with boundary information from the original footage, allowing for natural separation between the subject and background even around fine details such as hair. Park: Maintaining consistent results across different shooting conditions — including weather, lighting, subject movement, and distance — was crucial. We repeatedly filmed under a wide range of conditions and reviewed the results, improving unnatural elements through software optimization and additional AI training data. Building on Samsung Research’s technology, image quality experts from the MX Business also evaluated the results from a user perspective, further refining the feature. ▲ Portrait Video recognizes faces and naturally shifts focus to another person when the main subject turns away. Q. What did it take to make this complex video processing reliable and ready for use on the Galaxy Z series? Kim: The biggest hurdle was reducing power consumption and heat generation without compromising quality. Video is a rapid sequence of images, so processing 4K video in real time requires significant computation. That meant we had to prioritize. We preserved the processing essential to image quality while reducing computation in areas where users were unlikely to notice a difference. As a result, we struck a balance between natural lens rendering and real-time processing, ensuring stable, efficient performance even during extended recording. More Freedom in Video Creation Q. What are some tips to help users get the most out of Portrait Video? Kim: To make bokeh stand out, look for scenes with bright light sources against a relatively dark background. Sunlight sparkling through leaves, Christmas lights, or streetlights at night can spread softly into circular Bokeh, creating a more atmospheric look. When filming a person, it’s best to avoid strong light from the front. Instead, position the light source behind or to the side of the subject. This can softly illuminate the subject’s hair and contours while making the background Bokeh more prominent. Reflected light or ambient sources like streetlights can help keep the face from getting too dark for a more balanced result. ▲ An object filmed at a café using Portrait Video. The naturally blurred background makes the subject stand out. Q. What reaction would you most like to hear from people who have tried Portrait Video? Park: I’d like users, creators, and video professionals to be surprised by how easy it is to create cinematic video on a smartphone. I hope the natural blur, Bokeh, and post-capture editing features give them greater freedom to achieve the look and feel they want. Kim: Ultimately, I hope people feel they no longer need to carry a separate professional camera. We will continue advancing the underlying technologies so they can create cinematic videos with just a smartphone. ▲ The experts look forward to what’s next for Portrait Video. Bringing the cinematic shallow depth of field and light rendering of professional camera lenses to smartphone video required extensive testing and collaboration to turn a research concept into a reliable product feature. Developed through the combined expertise of Samsung Research and the MX Business, Portrait Video expands the Galaxy video experience — giving users more ways to realize their creative vision. The shape and texture of blur in out-of-focus areas, often seen when small points of light appear as circular highlights. ︎ A lens with an aperture that can open wide to let in more light, making it well suited for keeping the subject sharp while softly blurring the background and rendering bokeh highlights. ︎
